name: Woccon
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: extinct; attested only via Lawson's 1711 143-word list; no prosodic documentation possible

sources.citation: Lawson, John. 1709. A New Voyage to Carolina. London. Vocabulary of Tuskeruro, Pampticough and Woccon, pp. 225-230.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The only primary record of the language: ~143 English glosses with Woccon forms in Lawson's ad-hoc English spelling; hyphens mark syllable breaks (Num-perre, Nam-mee, Yau-hauk) but there are no accent marks anywhere in the vocabulary (0 accented vowels in the scanned of pp. 225-230) and no remark on accent or pronunciation; the only framing sentence is 'And here I shall insert a small Dictionary of every Tongue, though not Alphabetically digested.'
143-word Lawson list plus Adelung & Vater's 16 glosses; 'limited and inconsistent nature of the data makes identifying grammatical patterns.. extremely difficult'; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Passmore, Elizabeth, Sayers, Ann, Bradley, Jacob & Lomboy, Ashley. 2024. Reviving Waccamaw Siouan: Reconciling ethics, Indigenous epistemologies, and colonial data archives. Proceedings of the Linguistic Society of America 9(1): 5717. doi:10.3765/plsa.v9i1.5717
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Identifies Woccon with Waccamaw Siouan; states the only data are Lawson's 143-word list and Adelung & Vater's 16 glosses, 'This paucity of language data makes it difficult to identify linguistic patterns in the data'; notes Lawson's claim of no l or f sounds contradicted by his spellings; no statement on stress, accent or prosody (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).

sources.citation: Living Tongues Institute / Skarure Woccon Nation. 2021-. Woccon Living Dictionary, About page.
sources.note: About page (https://livingdictionaries.app/woccon/about): data = ~140 words from Lawson 1709 plus Carter 1980 and Rudes 2000 as sources; 'The next phase of work will include working with Siouan linguistics specialists to determine the correct pronunciation of the Woccon terms.' Entries/grammar pages are a JS app and did not render; no stress information.

sources.citation: Adelung, Johann Christoph & Vater, Johann Severin. 1816. Mithridates oder allgemeine Sprachenkunde, vol. 3 pt 3, sect. C 'Woccons, Katahba', pp. 306-308. Berlin: Vossische Buchhandlung.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnohistorical paragraph ('Die Woccons oder Waccons kennen wir blos aus Lawson's new voyage on Carolina (Lond. 1709)') plus a handful of Woccon-Katahba word comparisons (Schnee, Hund, Wasser) copied from Lawson; nothing on accent.

sources.citation: Rudes, Blair A. 2003. Catawba Phonemes. In Rudes & Costa (eds.), Essays in Algonquian, Catawban and Siouan Linguistics in Memory of Frank T. Siebert, Jr. (Algonquian and Iroquoian Linguistics Memoir 16), 217-254. Winnipeg.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PM601.E85 2003); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PM601 .E85 2003
sources.note: Sister-language stress rule (weight-sensitive penult/antepenult; already held under cata1286 as OL snippets) is the only basis any reconstitution of Woccon accent could rest on; a full copy would show whether Rudes extends the rule to Woccon.

sources.citation: Rudes, Blair A. 2000. Resurrecting coastal Catawban: The reconstituted phonology and morphology of the Woccon language. Southern Journal of Linguistics 24(2): 228-244.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only phonological treatment of Woccon in existence (HNAI 14: 'Rudes (2000) examines the phonology and morphology'); if any accent placement was projected onto Woccon from Catawba's weight-sensitive penult/antepenult system (Rudes 2003), it would be here. No open copy; SECOL journal not digitized.

sources.citation: Rudes, Blair A. 1985. The Universal versus the Particular, and the Case of Woccon Number Words. IJAL 51(4): 566-568.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: Short note on Woccon numerals with Rudes's phonological reading of Lawson's forms; low chance of a stress remark but it is one of only three analytic works on the language.

sources.citation: Carter, Richard T. 1980. The Woccon Language of North Carolina: Its Genetic Affiliations and Historical Significance. IJAL 46(3): 170-182.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: Comparative-historical study; principal modern analysis of Lawson's list with phonological correspondences to Catawba and Siouan; would confirm whether any prosodic inference was drawn from Lawson's spellings.
